# Cards the DSL cannot say yet

Every card here was read by an authoring worker that judged it *not expressible*
and declined to approximate it — see [card-authoring.md](card-authoring.md). The
grouping is the point: one card that did not work is an anecdote, and seventy
waiting on the same missing mechanic is a build order.

Clear the top entry with `/extend-dsl <capability>`, then re-run
`python scripts/author_cards.py --tier templates --retry` to harvest what it unblocks.

## prevent-damage-by-source

Blocks **8** cards.

- **(static_effect)** a `prevent_damage` static (prevent_all, combat_only, affects self_only) that also filters the damage's SOURCE, and a source filter meaning 'a creature blocking this permanent' (blocking the source of the static specifically, not any blocking creature)
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `prevent_damage` with `combat_only` + `prevent_all` + `affects: {self_only: true}` prevents ALL combat damage to the creature, which is strictly better than printed (it would also stop damage from creatures it is blocking, if it blocks). `damage_source` exists but the loader refuses it on anything but `replace_damage`, and the static filter key `blocking` is a boolean ('is blocking'), not 'is blocking this creature', so even on a source filter it could not say 'blocking it'.
- **(static_effect)** a source filter on the `prevent_damage` static (prevent_all + combat_only + affects self_only) restricting the shield to damage dealt by sources matching a filter, e.g. a dealer filter of {"enchanted_by": true} (a creature with at least one Aura attached to it)
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The `prevent_damage` static's `combat_only` + `prevent_all` read only the recipient (`affects`), never the dealer, so it would prevent combat damage from every creature. `damage_source` filters the dealer but is honoured only by `replace_damage` (a multiplier), not by prevention. The `enchanted_by` filter key says 'enchanted creatures'; nothing lets the prevention shield read it of the dealer.
- **(static_effect)** a dealer-side total shield on the `prevent_damage` static: `{"effect": "prevent_damage", "prevent_all": true, "combat_only": true, "damage_source": {"self_only": true}}` preventing all combat damage this creature would deal to any recipient (creatures, players and planeswalkers). The 'dealt to' half is already expressible as a second `prevent_damage` static with `prevent_all`, `combat_only` and `affects: {"self_only": true}`
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The loader accepts `damage_source` on `prevent_damage` only beside `affects_player` with no `affects`, and refuses `prevent_all` beside `affects_player`; the player-side reader (`prevented_player_damage`) skips `prevent_all` statics and only absorbs N. So there is no way to prevent all damage dealt BY a source. `replace_damage` filters by `damage_source` but only multiplies or adds, it cannot prevent. Writing only the 'dealt to' half would leave Fog Bank dealing combat damage, a different card.
- **(static_effect)** a damage_source (dealer) filter on the prevent_damage static, so 'prevent all combat damage that would be dealt by enchanted creature' is {effect: prevent_damage, prevent_all: true, combat_only: true, damage_source: {attached: true}} -- prevention keyed on the source rather than the recipient, applied wherever combat damage is dealt (to players and permanents alike)

- **(op)** an op that grants escape until end of turn to one targeted card in a graveyard: the card may be cast from the graveyard this turn for its own mana cost plus an additional cost of exiling N other cards from its owner's graveyard (N=2 here), with the escaped condition readable afterwards
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: grant_playable with playable: this_turn lets the card be cast from the graveyard but carries no extra non-mana cost, so the 'exile two other cards from your graveyard' half would be dropped; grant_graveyard_cast is a player-wide permission over affects_spells (flashback-style), not a per-target grant with an exile_from_graveyard additional cost; the card-level graveyard_cost/graveyard_cast riders describe a card's own printed escape, not one granted to another card
- **(static_effect)** a granted escape permission: a `cast_from_graveyard`-style static (here `affects_spells: {"types": ["Enchantment"]}`) whose granted cast charges an additional cost on top of the card's own mana cost -- `exile_from_graveyard: {"count": 3}` where 'other' excludes the card being escaped, not the granting permanent -- priced and paid when the granted spell is cast, with no per-turn cap (the exile is the brake), and marking the spell as escaped (702.138) rather than exiling it on resolution, so an escaped enchantment returns to the graveyard and can escape again
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `cast_from_graveyard` grants the cast at the printed cost only, carries no additional-cost rider, and the loader requires `static_max_per_turn`, which this card does not print. The card-level `graveyard_cost` / `graveyard_additional_cost` slot is escape and can carry `exile_from_graveyard`, but it is set on the escaping card itself at load time; nothing writes a cost onto other cards. `grant_graveyard_cast` only takes `affects_spells`, `any_graveyard` and `grants_flashback` (flashback exiles the card, escape does not). `grant_keyword` has no escape keyword. Same blocker as underworld_breach.
- **(static_effect)** an additional-cost rider on the `cast_from_graveyard` static -- a Cost charged on top of the granted spell's own mana cost, drawn from `cost_keys`, so this card's static can carry `exile_from_graveyard: {"count": 3, "exclude_self": true}`. It must be priced and paid by `legality.graveyard_cast_permission` / `Game._cast` at the moment the granted spell is cast (the way `chosen_additional` charges a card's own `additional_cost`), and `exclude_self` has to mean the card being escaped, not the permanent granting the permission -- otherwise a three-card graveyard pays for the escape with the escaping card itself.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `cast_from_graveyard` is the only static that lets a card out of a graveyard and it grants the cast at the card's printed cost with no price attached. Its whole rider vocabulary is `enters_tapped`, `arrived_this_turn_from` and `affects_spells`; the one cost field on any permission static is `pay_life_instead`, which belongs to `cast_from_library_top`, swaps mana for life rather than adding to it, and cannot express an exile. The card-level `graveyard_cost` / `flashback` slot *is* escape and does carry `exile_from_graveyard` with `exclude_self` -- but it is a field on the escaping card itself, set at load time, and Underworld Breach hands escape to cards it has never seen. There is no op or static that writes a cost onto another card, and `grant_keyword` knows only the 34 ability keywords, none of which is escape.
- **(static_effect)** an unbounded `cast_from_graveyard` permission -- `static_max_per_turn` made optional (or given an explicit unlimited spelling) for permissions whose price is itself the rate limit, with `legality.graveyard_cast_permission` skipping the `GRAVEYARD_CAST_SLOT` ledger check instead of defaulting `cap` to 1. Underworld Breach prints no cap at all; the three exiled cards per cast are the whole brake.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The loader hard-refuses `cast_from_graveyard` without `static_max_per_turn` (`if not model.static_max_per_turn`), on the stated grounds that a permission with no rate limit is an unbounded engine rather than a printed line -- which is true of Edgar, Master Machinist's "once during each of your turns" and exactly false of this card. Every accepted value is a finite integer, so any number I could write would be a cap this card does not print: the card is a storm/loop enabler and an invented ceiling is the approximation, not a rounding of one.
- **(engine)** a verification sandbox that can cast an escape card for its escape cost from the graveyard (the card in the graveyard plus at least five other cards there), or an argued exception in the playable gate for a creature whose own 'sacrifice it unless it escaped' trigger lawfully bins it when cast from hand
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Every line is expressible: graveyard_cost {mana: {G}{G}{U}{U}, exile_from_graveyard: {count: 5, exclude_self: true}} + graveyard_cast: graveyard, a self_enters trigger with if {escaped: false} -> sacrifice self_only, and self_enters/attacks triggers with gain_life 3, draw 1, may put_onto_battlefield a land from hand. A dry run of verify() passes schema/compile/residual but fails the playable gate: '_cast' always casts from hand via build_sandbox (graveyard holds only 2 cards, so escape is unpayable), Uro correctly sacrifices itself, and _play_once allows a permanent only on the battlefield. Its docstring forbids widening that set and says the fix is a sandbox role, not a weaker gate. Dropping or inverting the sacrifice clause would be an approximation.

## basic-land-type-mana

Blocks **3** cards.

- **(engine)** Rule 305.6 -- a permanent with a basic land type has the matching intrinsic mana ability ({T}: Add {G} for Forest) by virtue of carrying the subtype, derived in the characteristics pipeline (characteristics.abilities_of) so that a Forest subtype granted by a static brings {T}: Add {G} with it, visible to legality, the payment solver and activation (and still subject to summoning sickness on a creature, 302.6).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The type change itself is sayable: the `add_subtype` static carries `types` as well as `subtypes` (characteristics.py layer-4 grant loop does `types.update(static.get("types"))`), so {"effect": "add_subtype", "affects": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "is_token": false}, "types": ["Land"], "subtypes": ["Forest"]} would make each nontoken creature a 'Creature Land -- Forest', and the first sentence is a self_only `set_pt` reading a count of lands you control. But the engine never derives a mana ability from a basic land subtype -- Forest's {T}: Add {G} is printed on the basic card in data/cards/basics.cards.json, and abilities_of returns printed plus statics-granted abilities only. So every creature would read as a Forest land and none could tap for {G}, which is the whole reason the card is played. A `grant_ability` static handing out {T}: Add {G} is unprinted text and the residual gate would have no line for it to claim. Same open gap as urborg_tomb_of_yawgmoth (and Dryad of the Ilysian Grove / Yavimaya, which already ship inert).
- **(engine)** Rule 305.6 -- a land that gains a basic land type gains the matching intrinsic mana ability ({T}: Add {W}/{U}/{B}/{R}/{G}), derived in the characteristics pipeline so an `add_subtype` grant of Plains/Island/Swamp/Mountain/Forest brings the mana abilities with it, visible to legality, the payment solver and activation.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The type change itself is sayable as {"effect": "add_subtype", "affects": {"types": ["Land"], "has_counters": ...}, "subtypes": [every land type in enums.SUBTYPE_CLASS]}, but the engine never derives a mana ability from a granted basic land type, so the land would be every land type in name only and tap for nothing new -- the main effect of the line. Same blocker as Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth and Ashaya.
- **(engine)** Rule 305.6 -- a land with a basic land type has the corresponding intrinsic mana ability ({T}: Add {W}/{U}/{B}/{R}/{G}) by virtue of carrying the subtype, derived in the characteristics pipeline (characteristics.abilities_of) rather than printed on the card, so that a subtype a static ability *grants* brings the mana ability with it. The derived ability must be visible to legality, the payment solver and activation, exactly as the `grant_ability` static already is.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The static effect `add_subtype` says the printed sentence exactly -- {"effect": "add_subtype", "affects": {"types": ["Land"], "controller": "any"}, "subtypes": ["Swamp"]} -- but the engine never derives a mana ability from a subtype. data/cards/basics.cards.json prints "{T}: Add {B}" on Swamp as an ordinary ability, and characteristics.abilities_of returns the printed list plus statics-granted abilities only; nothing consults subtypes. So the static loads clean, every land on the board correctly reads "Land -- Swamp", and not one of them can tap for {B} -- the whole reason the card is played. Urborg itself would also be a land with no mana ability at all, since its {T}: Add {B} is likewise only the 305.6 consequence of being a Swamp. The nearest workaround, a `grant_ability` static handing every land a {T}: Add {B} ability, is not what the card says: it would leave the lands not actually Swamps (invisible to swampwalk, domain, Swamp-fetching searches, and any "nonbasic land" test) while adding an ability the printed line never mentions, and the residual gate would have no printed sentence for it to claim. Dryad of the Ilysian Grove (data/cards/auto/templates.cards.json) already ships with the same construction and the same silent inertness, so closing this fixes both.

  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Timing is decided entirely by `legality._timing_ok` (src/commanderblitz/engine/legality.py), which returns True only for `card.is_instant` or `Keyword.FLASH.value in card.keywords` -- printed characteristics read off the CardDef -- and otherwise falls back to the sorcery-speed window from `_can_act_at_sorcery_speed`. It needs three new pieces -- a setup window that walks opening hands, a card-level spelling for the ability (a `begin_the_game` block, or an ability whose active_zones include `hand` with a game-start evaluation site), and a condition that can ask "you are not the starting player"
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_opening_sequence` (src/commanderblitz/engine/game.py) draws STARTING_HAND, runs London mulligans, and goes straight to turn 1; it never looks at what is in anyone's opening hand, so there is no window in which a card in hand can act at all. `active_zones` defaults to `(Zone.BATTLEFIELD,)` (src/commanderblitz/cards/loader/__init__.py) and the non-battlefield zones it is used for are graveyard/exile statics and activated abilities offered by `legality._activate_zones` -- both of which run once the game is already under way, so a HAND-zone ability would have no evaluator during setup. No entry in `trigger_events` is a game-start event: the earliest is `upkeep`, which is turn 1's upkeep and therefore after the starting player has already begun, and a trigger uses the stack rather than moving its own source out of hand. No entry in `condition_keys` asks who is on the play: `is_active_player` and `is_your_turn` are questions about the current turn, and both read true on the non-starting player's own turn, so neither can gate on "you're not the starting player". `put_onto_battlefield` can move a card, but it is a resolution op and there is nothing at setup to resolve it.

## activate-only-as-an-instant

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a timing restriction on an activated mana ability that bars it from being activated during the casting or cost-payment of a spell (rule 605.3a / the Lion's Eye Diamond ruling) while leaving it activatable whenever the player has priority: a flag legality and the mana solver both read, so costs.solver_taps and the payment planner never reach for it and only a priority activation can
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: 'sorcery_speed_only' is the opposite restriction -- it narrows activation to the main phase with an empty stack, where this line needs the *wider* instant timing minus the mid-cast window mana abilities uniquely get. 'activation_condition' is documented as a board question ('Activate only if you control five or more Vampires'), checked by legality against the game state, and cannot ask what the player is in the middle of doing. Nothing else in cost_keys or the ability fields describes when an ability may be activated. Dropping the sentence is not neutral: a plain is_mana_ability would be picked up by the solver while paying for another spell, so the engine would discard the player's hand on its own to help pay for a spell -- the precise thing the printed restriction forbids. The near-miss of setting is_mana_ability false hides it from the solver but pays a different price: the mana would then be produced on resolution from the stack, so the ability could be countered or responded to and could not be used to pay for a spell already being cast, which is the only reason anyone plays this card.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Lion's Eye Diamond** (rank 725) — `lion_s_eye_diamond`
  - Discard your hand, Sacrifice this artifact: Add three mana of any one color. Activate only as an instant.

</details>

## conditional-mana-ability

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a mana ability whose production is switched by a condition on its source at activation time -- "Add {C}; if this has a luck counter on it, instead add one mana of any color". `mana_options_of` and the payment solver must be able to evaluate a per-branch condition against live game state (here `counters_on` for a luck counter on the source) and offer only the branch that is currently true, in both the automatic tap path and the manual-mana path
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_split_mana_rider` (src/commanderblitz/cards/loader/mana.py) allows only leading `add_mana`/`choose_mode` effects plus a rider drawn from MANA_RIDER_OPS = {add_counters, add_poison, damage, gain_life, lose_life, remove_counters}; `if` is not in that set, so the printed conditional is a load error, not a card. `_mana_options` freezes production into a fixed tuple of 6-tuples at load time and `_mana_amount` may only scale one `add_mana`'s symbols, so no state can change *which* symbol is produced -- only how many. The three state-dependent forms that do exist (`mana_reflects`, `mana_identity`, `mana_chosen_color`) are each hardcoded questions about the board, the command zone or the permanent's chosen colour, and each is required to be the ability's only effect; none can be a condition on counters and none can pick between two branches. `choose_mode` is not a substitute and would be an approximation, because a mode is a free choice at activation: the land would offer any colour with no luck counter on it. Splitting the line into two mana abilities gated by `activation_condition` is silently wrong rather than merely ugly: `costs._sources_of` (src/commanderblitz/engine/costs.py) collects solver mana sources on `solver_taps` plus tapped/summoning-sickness/abilities_locked alone and never consults `activation_condition`, so the payment solver would happily tap the counter-less Caverns for any colour; `activation_condition` is only read on the offered-action path in `legality` (src/commanderblitz/engine/legality.py). It would also leave one printed line claimed by two abilities, which the residual gate reads as text nobody owns.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

  - If this card is in your opening hand and you're not the starting player, you may begin the game with Gemstone Caverns on the battlefield with a luck counter on it. If you do, exile a card from your hand.
  - {T}: Add {C}. If Gemstone Caverns has a luck counter on it, instead add one mana of any color.

</details>

## impulse-from-opponent-library

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a way to exile the top N cards of a *named* player's library and leave the impulse permission on the ability's controller rather than on that library's owner. Either a new key on look_at_top -- a 'playable_by' (or 'playable_controller') that makes _move_found write obj.playable_by = ctx.controller instead of the pid it looped over -- or, more generally, an 'as' binding on look_at_top recording the cards it moved (the way mill and exile already record theirs), so a following grant_playable can name them. Ragavan needs exactly one of these; with the binding, 'exile the top card of that player's library' becomes look_at_top {player: {binding: 'event_player'}, amount: 1, destination: 'exile', as: 'pilfered'} and 'until end of turn, you may cast that card' becomes grant_playable over {binding: 'pilfered'}
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: look_at_top is the only op that reaches the top of a library, and its playable_this_turn branch in effects/ops_cards.py _move_found hardcodes obj.playable_by = pid -- the player whose library was looked at. On Ragavan that library is the *opponent's*, so the printed 'you may cast that card' would grant the permission to the very player whose card was stolen: the opposite of the card. The exile op does set playable_by = ctx.controller, which is the right seat, but it takes a selector and selector_keys has no way to name the top of a library (no 'top'/'from_top' key; zone: 'library' with a count resolves to a chosen card from the whole deck, which is a tutor, not the top card). Composing the two also fails: look_at_top calls move_object without a 'by', so nothing records exiled_by and a follow-up grant_playable over {zone: 'exile', exiled_with: 'self'} matches nothing, while {zone: 'exile', player: ...} would match every card that player has ever had exiled. look_at_top has no 'as' binding either -- mill has one (Locke, Treasure Hunter) and exile has one, so this op is the odd one out. Naming 'that player' is NOT the gap: {"binding": "event_player"} already resolves to the damaged player, since primitives.damage_player fires COMBAT_DAMAGE_TO_PLAYER with player=pid.

## player-counter-replacement

Blocks **1** card.

- **(static_effect)** a replace_counters static that reaches only the controller as a player (affects_player: "you"), for every kind of player counter (poison and energy alike, no `counter`), without also reaching any permanent -- i.e. the loader should accept `affects_player` in place of `affects` on replace_counters, the way it already accepts `put_by` in place of it
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The loader refuses replace_counters without `affects` or `put_by`. Izzet Generatorium and Aether Refinery get away with a dummy `affects: {controller: you}` only because `counter: "energy"` keeps the static off permanents; with no counter kind ("one or more counters", "each of those kinds") that dummy affects would add a second +1 to every permanent you control, stacking with the first sentence on artifacts and creatures and wrongly reaching lands and enchantments. `put_by: "you"` is a different sentence (keyed on who puts the counters, not on you receiving them). The first sentence is expressible as replace_counters with counter_addend 1 and affects {any_types: [Artifact, Creature], controller: you}; the only non-gap spelling of the second would be an affects filter crafted to match no permanent (e.g. types [Instant]), which is a workaround rather than the printed sentence.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

  - If you would get one or more counters, you get that many plus one of each of those kinds of counters instead.

</details>

## same-target-for-each-target-word

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** rule 115.3: the same player or object may be chosen once for each instance of the word "target" on a spell, so Rush of Dread's three "target opponent" modes may all name one opponent; enumerate_target_tuples has to let separate specs of one spell share a ref (while one spec's own count still needs distinct choices)
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: targeting.enumerate_target_tuples drops any tuple in which two specs pick the same ref ("the same object cannot fill two targets"), so with spree_mode targets t1/t2/t3 every subset of two or more modes needs two or three different opponents: in a two-player game only single-mode casts exist, and at a pod each bought mode is forced onto a different opponent -- a different card. One shared spec is no fix: each mode's target opponent is chosen independently

## search-opponent-chooses

Blocks **1** card.

- **(decision)** a `chooser` on `search_library`/`search_zones` (a player spec, so it can be `{"target": ...}`) naming who picks from among the cards the search turned up -- the search itself is still performed and seen by the library's owner, but a *different*, targeted player makes the selection out of the revealed pool. Gifts Ungiven, Intuition and Plea for Power's kin all hang on it
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/ops_cards.py) hardcodes the asker: it iterates `select_players(ctx, spec.get("player", "you"))` and passes that same `pid` into `ask_objects(ctx, prompt, pool, 0, take, pid, "search")`, so the searcher is always the chooser. The selector's `chooser` key exists (selectors.py, and it accepts an arbitrary player spec) but a search never routes its selector through `pick_from_pool` -- the selector is only a match test via `_matches_in_zone` -- so writing `chooser` on a search's selector is silently ignored and the caster would pick their own card, which is the entire card. `two_piles` (ops_cards.py) is the only op whose first decision belongs to somebody else, and its splitter is `ctx.opponents()[0]` rather than a target, it reads `library[:amount]` off the top instead of a searched pool, and the *controller* still decides which pile is taken -- the opposite of "target opponent chooses one".

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Intuition** (rank 1971) — `intuition`
  - Target opponent chooses one.
  - Put that card into your hand and the rest into your graveyard.

</details>

## search-split-destinations

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a second destination on `search_library`/`search_zones` for the found-but-not-chosen cards (e.g. `destination: "hand"` plus `rest: "graveyard"`), so one search reveals N, a chosen subset goes one place and the remainder another, with the shuffle still happening once at the end
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` resolves one `DESTINATIONS[spec.get("destination", "hand")]` and hands every picked card to `_move_found` (ops_cards.py); cards that were revealed and not taken simply stay in the library. `look_at_top` is the only lookup with a remainder key, `rest_to_bottom` (ops_cards.py), and it is a boolean hardwired to `_bottom_in_random_order` -- bottom of library, never the graveyard -- besides reading the top N rather than searching. `two_piles` does carry `to`/`other`, but only over the top of the library and only as a pile split. Sequencing two ops instead is an approximation, not the card: `search_library` to the graveyard followed by a `return_from_graveyard` would put all three cards through the graveyard, firing `leaves_graveyard` and inflating `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` from 2 to 3, and `search_library` to hand followed by a `discard` would emit two `discard` events (madness, discard triggers) for cards the printing never discards.

## spells-cast-per-player

Blocks **1** card.

- **(value)** a value leaf that reports spells cast this turn *per player* rather than summed -- e.g. a `max_spells_cast_of: "each_opponent"`, or a per-player quantifier over a condition -- so "if **an opponent** cast three or more spells this turn" asks whether any single opponent reached three. Wanted by the whole Trap cycle and by storm-watching cards (Mindbreak Trap, Archmage Ascension-style counters, Guttersnipe-adjacent per-seat thresholds).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `alternative_cost` with `{"mana": "{0}"}` and a `condition` is exactly the right home for this line -- that half is not the blocker. The condition itself is: `spells_cast_this_turn` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/values.py) resolves its player spec through `select_players` and then **sums** the ledger across every seat it names, so `{"spells_cast_this_turn": "each_opponent"}` is the *total* spells cast by all opponents. At a pod that is a strictly wider card than the printing: three opponents casting one spell each would switch on the free cast, which Mindbreak Trap does not do. The per-player machinery that exists, `max_count_of`/`min_count_of` via `_counts_per_player` (values.py), counts *objects* matching a selector one seat at a time and has no reach into the turn ledger's `spells_cast`; `condition_keys`' `any`/`all` combine sibling conditions and do not quantify over players.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

</details>

- **(selector)** a group constraint on a variable-count target spec requiring all chosen targets to have the same value of a characteristic (here equal toughness), checked when targets are chosen and rechecked on resolution
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: target_keys carry count/min_count/up_to and the group caps total_power and total_mana_value, but nothing that ties the targets to one another by an equal toughness; a fixed `toughness` in the selector would pick a single number instead of letting the caster choose any shared value, and destroying with no constraint would let differing-toughness creatures be chosen

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **V.A.T.S.** (rank 4421) — `v_a_t_s`
  - Choose any number of target creatures with equal toughness. Destroy the chosen creatures.

</details>

## teammates

## x-sized-linked-targets

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** An X-sized spell target (count {"x": true}) whose selector names a sibling target declared before it -- {"kind": "card_in_graveyard", "count": {"x": true}, "selector": {"zone": "graveyard", "player": {"target": "graveyard_owner"}}} after a {"kind": "player"} target -- so the X cards are chosen from the graveyard of the player already picked. Dropping the link (controller "any") would let the X cards come from several graveyards, which is a different card
